_meta.source: Hand-curated from the sources listed per event
notes: Attributed means the cited source ties the event to El Niño; consistent means the source does not name El Niño, but the event fits the known El Niño pattern for that region.
Coverage is a selection of well-sourced reports from March to September 2026, not a complete count of El Niño impacts.

28 Sep 2026: 25 more events added after a coverage audit (Australia had none; the Philippines, mainland South-East Asia and southern Africa were thin), each opened and checked by a second reader; quote holds the sentence checked.
30 Sep 2026: Panama easing (ACP A-36-2026) added; it is marked consistent because the advisory does not name El Niño.

events.title: Rains linked to coastal El Niño kill 92 in Peru, displace over 23,000
events.place: Across Peru: the north coast (Piura, Tumbes) plus Andean and Amazon regions
events.impact: 92 deaths and more than 23,000 people displaced by floods, landslides and river overflows since January, as of 17 March (UN OCHA figures).
events.why: ECHO says the rains are linked to the coastal El Niño, and Peru's national El Niño commission kept its coastal El Niño alert in force.

source.title: Peru – Severe weather, floods and landslides, update (UN OCHA, NOAA-CPC) (ECHO Daily Flash of 24 March 2026)

events.title: Ecuador floods destroy 8,350 ha of crops under a national emergency
events.impact: 71,309 people affected, 6,066 displaced and 14 dead since January; 8,350 ha of crops destroyed and more than 126,000 animals killed, as of 22 March. National state of emergency since 12 March.
events.why: The source does not name El Niño for Ecuador. Heavy wet-season rain on this coast is the coastal El Niño pattern in the region list, and the Niño 1+2 sea box averaged 1.5 °C above its 1971 to 2000 normal in March 2026 (NOAA OISST).

source.title: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 23 March 2026

events.title: Peru opens anchovy season early, fearing coastal El Niño
events.place: North-Central anchovy fishing zone, off Peru's north and central coast
events.impact: The season opened on 1 April, about two weeks before the usual mid-April start, after the industry warned coastal El Niño warming would scatter the fish.
events.why: The source says forecasts of a coastal El Niño led the fishing industry to push for an early start, before the sea grew too warm to find fish. It does not tie the lower quota to El Niño.

source.title: Peru launches first North-Central anchovy season of 2026 with decreased TAC of 1.9 million tons

events.title: Honduras appeals for aid as Dry Corridor drought deepens
events.place: El Paraíso and Francisco Morazán, Honduras
events.impact: May to August rain in El Paraíso and Francisco Morazán ran 39% below average, the second lowest in 35 years; 233 of 298 municipalities were on drought alert by 16 Sep, 103 at red.
events.why: The appeal names El Niño only as a risk for the months ahead, not as the cause; a dry July to August canícula in the Dry Corridor is the published El Niño pattern.

source.title: Honduras: Drought Flash Appeal - Sep 2026

events.title: Peru pauses anchovy fishing over a high share of juveniles
events.place: North-Central anchovy fishing zone, off Peru's north and central coast
events.impact: Fishing paused on 12 May and the pause was extended to 10 June over a high share of juveniles; 453,000 tonnes, 24% of the 1.9 million tonne quota, had been landed by then.
events.why: The source reports the pause alongside coastal El Niño warming that it says has already changed the behaviour and distribution of anchovy. It gives juveniles, not El Niño, as the direct reason for the pause.

source.title: Peru extends pause to anchovy fishing as El Niño threats continue to loom large

events.title: Cattle die as drought grips Central America's Dry Corridor
events.impact: About 100 cows died in recent months in San Lorenzo, Honduras; some Guatemalan villagers pay 50% above normal for corn.
events.why: AFP ties the drought to this year's El Niño; a dry canícula is the known El Niño pattern here.

source.title: Dead animals, barren fields, and hunger - El Nino chokes Central America

events.title: Driest kiremt start on record in central Ethiopia
events.impact: Rain deficits above 100 mm in places by 20 June, the driest season start on record in central Tigray, Amhara and Oromia; in Tigray, under half the average long-cycle crop area was planted.
events.why: FEWS NET expects the ongoing El Niño to bring below-average June to September kiremt rain, the season behind most of Ethiopia's harvest.

source.title: Peak lean season emerges as El Niño stalls kiremt rains, risking seasonal recovery

events.title: India's June monsoon rain falls 40% short
events.impact: 40% below normal June rain across India; central India was 50% below normal, the largest shortfall of any region.
events.why: Down To Earth names El Niño as one expected reason for the June deficit; El Niño usually suppresses India's June to September monsoon.

source.title: Imprint of El Nino, other weather patterns on India's deficit June 2026 rainfall

events.title: India heads for driest monsoon since 2009 as El Niño curbs rain
events.impact: 15% below the long-term average: India's June to September rain so far, per IMD; rice, sugar cane and corn plantings trail last season.
events.why: Bloomberg ties the shortfall to a strengthening El Niño, which is known to weaken the monsoon.

source.title: India on track for driest monsoon in 17 years as El Nino curbs rain

events.title: Poor rains leave Sudan's sorghum belt in severe drought
events.impact: Up to 70% of cropland in Gedaref and 55% in Sennar in severe drought; seasonal rain ran about 30% (Gedaref) and 20% (Sennar) below the long-term average.
events.why: FAO GIEWS links the below-average rains to the ongoing El Niño event.

source.title: GIEWS Country Brief: The Republic of the Sudan 24-September-2026

events.title: Rain under 45% of average in parts of South Sudan, Sudan and Ethiopia
events.place: South Sudan, northwestern Sudan and Ethiopia's kiremt regions
events.impact: Many areas got under 45% of average rain from 1 June to 10 July across South Sudan, northwestern Sudan and the kiremt regions of western, central, northern and northeastern Ethiopia.
events.why: FEWS NET says El Niño conditions typically suppress the June to September rains in western and northern East Africa.

source.title: Deepening concerns across East Africa following severe June rainfall deficits and forecast below-average July–September rains

events.title: Drought hits 226,774 ha of Guatemalan farmland, most in a decade
events.impact: 226,774 ha hit by agricultural drought by 27 August, the most in a decade; 221,772 ha of it maize, 22.5% of the national maize area. Jalapa (57,582 ha) and Jutiapa (49,465 ha) were hit hardest.
events.why: The agriculture ministry reports a canícula of about 60 days without significant rain in July and August. The article does not name El Niño for 2026, but a long canícula is the Dry Corridor's El Niño signal.

source.title: La sequía agrícola afecta 226.773,97 hectáreas en Guatemala y supera el registro de la última década

events.title: Sudan's rains arrive up to a month late in Darfur and Kordofan
events.impact: Rains 20 to 30 days late in North Darfur and North Kordofan; with forecasts to mid-August, parts rank driest in 40 years of records.
events.why: FEWS NET says El Niño-linked below-average rains are expected to limit harvests in western Sudan.

source.title: Conflict and poor rainfall to drive Emergency and risk of Famine through January

events.title: Rivers and streams dry up in four Solomon Islands provinces
events.place: Malaita, Makira, Choiseul and Western provinces
events.impact: Rivers, streams and other water sources drying up in 4 provinces: Malaita, Makira, Choiseul and Western.
events.why: ABC reports that a major El Niño is causing the rivers and streams to dry up.

source.title: River levels drop across the Solomons due to El Nino

events.title: Kharif planting in India runs 20% behind last year
events.impact: 35 million ha sown by early July vs 44.3 million ha a year earlier; oilseed area fell nearly 40%, from 10.9 to 6.6 million ha.
events.why: Down To Earth says the dry spell coincided with strengthening El Niño conditions and asks in its headline whether El Niño is the cause.

source.title: El Niño impact? Monsoon rainfall deficit slows kharif sowing across India, leaving planting 20% behind last year

events.title: Peru's anchovy landings down 80% as coastal waters warm
events.impact: 471,000 t landed so far vs 2.3 million t by the same point in 2025, an 80% drop and about 25% of the 1.9 million t quota; the first north-central season is suspended.
events.why: RPP says El Niño Costero has hit industrial fishing since May and has forced the first season to be suspended.

source.title: Pesca peruana en jaque por fenómeno El Niño: desembarques de anchoveta caen 80% y peligra toda la temporada 2026

events.title: Winter storm floods ten regions of Chile
events.place: Ten regions of Chile, worst in Coquimbo, Huasco province and Tierra Amarilla
events.impact: 13 dead, 4 missing, more than 3,500 people with damaged homes and at least 61,000 cut off; more than 176,000 power customers still out in Coquimbo.
events.why: CNN says the frontal system was favoured by El Niño; wetter winters in north-central Chile are a known El Niño effect.
events.quote: Favorecido por el fenómeno de El Niño, un sistema frontal afectó a diez regiones del país austral

source.title: Intensas lluvias en Chile dejan al menos 13 muertos y más de 3.500 de damnificados

events.title: Warm coastal water pushes Peru's anchoveta close to shore
events.impact: 10 nautical miles: IMARPE's 16 to 30 July survey found north-central anchoveta packed within 10 nm of shore, south of Salaverry, deeper than normal.
events.why: ENFEN says the coastal El Niño will keep affecting fishing and where species are found; anchoveta losses are Peru's best-documented El Niño harm.

source.title: Impacto en el mar peruano: El Niño Costero seguirá afectando a la pesca y la distribución de especies en los próximos meses

events.title: Rio Grande do Sul has its first big flood of this El Niño
events.place: Taquari and Caí valleys, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
events.impact: The Taquari reached 20.8 m at Lajeado against a 19 m flood level after 100 to 200 mm of rain in the Taquari and Caí basins.
events.why: MetSul Meteorologia calls the flood the first big one linked to the 2026-27 El Niño; southern Brazil usually gets more rain in El Niño years.
events.quote: O Rio Grande do Sul amanheceu nesta quarta-feira (22/7) sob a primeira grande enchente associada ao Super El Niño 2026-2027.

source.title: MetSul: enchente no RS é o primeiro efeito do Super El Niño no Brasil

events.title: Local rain deficits and dry spells stress Sahel millet
events.place: Western and central Sahel: Mauritania, Senegal, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Chad and Burkina Faso
events.impact: Severe local deficits, in places with dry spells of more than 8 days; millet met under 70% of its water needs in parts of southern Mauritania, central Mali, western Niger and central Chad.
events.why: FEWS NET does not name El Niño in this monitor; a poor July to September rainy season in the Sahel is a known El Niño pattern.
events.quote: The most extensive severe deficits are concentrated in western Mauritania, northern Senegal, eastern Mali, western Niger, southwestern Nigeria, and parts of central Chad

source.title: Rainy season progresses with localized deficits across the Sahel

events.title: Vanuatu declares drought in its northern provinces
events.place: Torba, with parts of Sanma, Penama and Malampa
events.impact: 3 months of low rain: all of Torba and parts of Sanma, Penama and Malampa provinces declared in drought.
events.why: The report says the dry conditions are driven by the arrival of El Niño.

source.title: Vanuatu declares drought in northern areas as El Nino brings dry weather

events.title: Indonesia: 1,637 sites go over 60 days without rain
events.impact: 1,637 observation points in 25 provinces had more than 60 days without rain; Bantul went 131 days, BMKG data show.
events.why: BMKG calls the drought an El Niño impact, made worse by the Indian Ocean Dipole.

source.title: Ribuan Titik di RI Tak Diguyur Hujan Lebih dari 2 Bulan Imbas El Nino

events.title: Panama Canal cuts ship draft again as Gatun Lake falls
events.impact: Maximum draft cut from 49.5 ft in early July to 49.0 ft on 24 July and 48.5 ft on 15 August; a 48.0 ft limit set for 26 August was postponed on 20 August.
events.why: gCaptain reports the cuts amid a strengthening El Niño that NOAA says raises the risk of below-normal rain across Central America.

source.title: Panama Canal to Tighten Draft Limits Again as Water Levels Continue to Fall

events.title: Parts of southern inland Queensland drought declared for the first time in two years
events.place: Balonne, Goondiwindi, Southern Downs and southern Maranoa, Queensland, Australia
events.impact: Four council areas drought declared after 12 months or more of well below average rain and pasture growth; interest-free drought loans of up to $50,000 and $250,000 reinstated.
events.why: The declaration does not name El Niño, and the 12-month rain deficit began before El Niño set in; a dry winter in inland eastern Australia fits the usual El Niño pattern.
events.quote: The LGAs of Balonne, Goondiwindi, Southern Downs, and the southern part of Maranoa have been drought-declared

source.title: Queensland prepared as drought declared in parts of the southern inland

events.title: Tasmania has its driest August since 1982 and its warmest August days on record
events.impact: 82.6 mm of rain, 44% below the 1961 to 1990 average and the seventh-driest August since 1900; state mean maximum of 12.4 C, the warmest August on record since 1910.
events.why: The Bureau of Meteorology summary does not name El Niño; a dry, warm late winter in south-east Australia fits the usual El Niño pattern.
events.quote: Tasmania's area-averaged rainfall total in August was 82.6 mm, 44% below the 1961–1990 average, the seventh-driest on record for all Augusts since 1900.

source.title: Tasmania in August 2026

events.title: Ethiopia's meher harvest could be up to 30% below average
events.place: East and West Hararghe lowlands, central and eastern Tigray, northeastern Amhara
events.impact: Meher harvest could be up to 30% below average; kiremt rain under 60% of average in eastern Tigray, northern Afar, northern Somali, Sidama and South Ethiopia; little to no meher crop expected in the East and West Hararghe lowlands.
events.why: FEWS NET's August update links the historically poor kiremt rains to El Niño.

source.title: Historically poor kiremt rainfall linked to El Niño drives meher crop losses

events.title: Drought spreads in northern NSW and turns intense around Dungog
events.place: Northern NSW, the Hunter and the south coast, New South Wales, Australia
events.impact: The NSW drought index shows the Drought category expanding in the north, areas around Dungog moving to Intense Drought, drought emerging on the south coast and eastern Monaro, and many farm dams under 20% water cover.
events.why: NSW DPIRD ties the drought to long-term rain deficits and does not blame El Niño for it; it says a strong El Niño, with a possible positive IOD, raises the odds of a hotter, drier spring.
events.quote: drought conditions persist across large parts of northern and northeastern NSW, where winter rainfall has been insufficient to alleviate long-term deficits

source.title: Drought to Intensify in Northern NSW
source.publisher: STA FM, republishing the NSW DPIRD seasonal update media release

events.title: El Salvador declares a national red alert for drought
events.place: Eastern El Salvador (Santa Rosa de Lima)
events.impact: 14 heat records in August, up to 43.9°C in Santa Rosa de Lima, and up to 19 dry days in a row since 7 August; national red alert declared.
events.why: Civil Protection says conditions are strongly influenced by El Niño.

source.title: Declaratoria de alerta roja por sequía meteorológica y agrícola 25/agosto/2026
source.publisher: Dirección General de Protección Civil, El Salvador

events.title: Fires and drought hit Tolima farms in Colombia
events.impact: 31,000+ hectares of Tolima affected as of 26 Aug, per Cortolima; farmers are losing mango, avocado and plantain to fire and drought.
events.why: El Espectador ties the fires and crop losses in Tolima to the strongest El Niño in years.

source.title: El Niño más fuerte en años pone contra las cuerdas al campo y a miles de productores

events.title: Indonesia: 48,890 ha of peatland ablaze in Sumatra and Borneo
events.place: Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, Central and South Kalimantan
events.impact: 48,890 ha of peatland ablaze in Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, Central and South Kalimantan; nearly 50,000 firefighters and disaster staff deployed.
events.why: Indonesia's coordinating minister for political and security affairs said stronger El Niño conditions raised the risk of fires in the peak dry season.

source.title: Wildfires burn across Indonesia as officials cite El Nino as a cause

events.title: Honduras puts 234 of 298 municipalities on drought alert
events.impact: 234 of 298 municipalities on drought alert, 75 of them at red, after low reservoir levels, crop losses and livestock deaths; Tegucigalpa tops the red list.
events.why: AFP reports El Niño scorching harvests and killing livestock; the Dry Corridor is the worst-hit area.

source.title: Honduras places 80% of country on El Nino drought alert

events.title: Haze from Indonesian fires reaches hazardous levels in Sarawak
events.impact: Air Pollutant Index hit 407 in Kuching; nearly 600 schools shut on 20 and 21 August; weekly asthma cases in Malaysia rose from 219 to 1,811.
events.why: ASEAN raised its top haze alert, citing more fire hotspots and prolonged dry weather fuelled by an intensifying El Niño.
events.quote: ASEAN cited an increase in fire hotspots and prolonged dry weather, fuelled by an intensifying El Nino weather pattern.

source.title: Toxic haze from Indonesian forest fires chokes Malaysian Borneo

events.title: Eastern Australia's wheat states get a quarter of normal rain or less in 30 days
events.place: Wheat belt of Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria, Australia
events.impact: From 22 August to 20 September, Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria got no more than 25% of normal rain; South Australia was similarly dry.
events.why: DTN calls a drier trend in Australian wheat areas one of El Niño's strongest effects and says this pattern is typical of El Niño.
events.quote: This drier pattern is typical of El Nino's impact

source.title: El Nino-Related Dryness Could Reduce Australia Wheat Production

events.title: Papua New Guinea drought turns critical in Western Province
events.impact: 3 provinces in drought: NCD and Gulf remain in drought and Western Province turned drought critical at the three-month scale.
events.why: PNG's weather service puts 'El Niño is firmly established and strengthening' in the key messages of this drought update.

source.title: Papua New Guinea Climate and Special Services: September 2026 Drought Update
source.publisher: Government of Papua New Guinea (via ReliefWeb)

events.title: ABARES cuts Queensland winter crop forecast 44% as the north stays dry
events.place: Queensland and northern New South Wales cropping regions, Australia
events.impact: Queensland winter crop forecast down 44% to 2.2 million tonnes and New South Wales down 30% to 13.1 million tonnes; national chickpea output forecast down 52%.
events.why: ABARES blames low stored soil moisture and limited winter rain and does not name El Niño in this report; a dry winter in northern NSW and Queensland fits the usual El Niño pattern.
events.quote: conditions in northern New South Wales and most of Queensland are poor with a significant decline in the area planted and below average yield expectations

source.title: Australian Crop Report September 2026
source.publisher: ABARES, Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry

events.title: Panama Canal cuts transits and draft as El Niño dries watershed
events.impact: 34 daily transit slots from 3 Sep (9 Neopanamax, 25 Panamax), Panamax cut to 23 on 15 Sep; Neopanamax draft capped at 48 ft from 2 Sep.
events.why: The Canal Authority cites the El Niño event and below-expected rain in the canal watershed.

source.title: Panama Canal Authority Adopts New Transit Restrictions

events.title: Typhoon Saudel floods coastal Fujian
events.impact: Floods in Fuding and Putian, a three-storey house collapsed in Jinxi village, some people missing, and more than 83,000 people evacuated in Fujian alone.
events.why: Reuters reports experts saying this rare run of typhoons is closely linked to El Niño.
events.quote: The meteorological sequence is extremely rare, according to the China Meteorological Administration, and one that experts say is closely linked to El Niño.

source.title: Typhoon Saudel Brings Torrential Rain, Flooding to China's Coastal Areas

events.title: Rainy-season dry spell withers rice in Lampang, northern Thailand
events.place: Mae Wa, Thoen district, Lampang, Thailand
events.impact: Rice on roughly 320 to 480 hectares outside irrigation zones is drying out; officials are handing out water to households and warn the area's whole rice crop could be lost without rain.
events.why: Thai PBS reports the dry spell as an effect of El Niño.
events.quote: The lingering effects of the El Niño weather phenomenon are taking a heavy toll on northern farmers

source.title: El Niño dry spell leaves Lampang rice crops withering

events.title: Early spring heat and bushfires hit south-east Queensland and northern NSW
events.place: South-east Queensland and Tabulam, northern New South Wales, Australia
events.impact: Brisbane reached 34.4 C, its hottest September day since 2019; around a dozen bushfires still active in Queensland and an emergency warning, later downgraded, for a grass fire near Tabulam.
events.why: The Bureau of Meteorology's Jonathon Howe told AAP a strengthening El Niño and unusually warm oceans are locking in very warm temperatures, especially in the east.
events.quote: He said a strengthening El Niño, combined with unusually warm oceans, was "locking in very warm temperatures right across the country"

source.title: Fires, heat and looming El Niño menace east coast

events.title: Dry weather hits more than 115,000 people in Sri Lanka
events.place: Seven districts of Sri Lanka, worst in Monaragala, Batticaloa, Badulla and Ampara
events.impact: 115,534 people affected and drinking water trucked to 113,354 people; Monaragala is worst hit with 41,360 people.
events.why: Sri Lanka's National Disaster Relief Services Center, quoted by Xinhua, links the dry weather to El Niño.
events.quote: affected by prevailing dry weather conditions linked to the El Nino weather pattern

source.title: Dry weather affects over 115,000 people in Sri Lanka

events.title: Surf from Marie's remnants erodes Southern California beaches
events.place: Long Beach to Orange County coast, California
events.impact: More than 12 oceanfront homes in Orange County severely damaged, at least one marked for demolition, after Marie's remnants hit in early September.
events.why: Bloomberg says El Niño has been supercharging Pacific storms that sent heavy surf to the West Coast.

source.title: California's El Nino emergency begins now as beaches erode

events.title: Hurricane Lowell batters Hawaii in a busy El Niño season
events.impact: 510+ homes destroyed or damaged and $168 million in public infrastructure damage from Hurricanes Lala (August) and Lowell (early September).
events.why: NOAA's lead hurricane season forecaster told AP that El Niño has brought four more tropical storms than normal to the eastern and central Pacific.

source.title: It's been an intense hurricane season in the Pacific and there's still a long way to go

events.title: Remote Fiji islands ask for drinking water
events.place: Vanua Levu, Taveuni and outer islands, Fiji
events.impact: Remote islands asking for drinking water; Fiji's rainfall watch lists seriously dry conditions in Taveuni and Cikobia and very dry conditions across Vanua Levu, Gau, parts of Koro and the northern Lau Group.
events.why: The director of the Fiji Meteorological Service ties the water requests to El Niño conditions.
events.quote: Some of Fiji’s remote islands have started asking for water as El Niño conditions begin putting pressure on drinking water supplies.

source.title: Remote islands seek water as El Niño conditions bite

events.title: El Niño-linked rain floods parts of Mogadishu
events.impact: 1 IRC-supported clinic, the Ariif Health Centre, disrupted as heavy rain linked to El Niño flooded parts of Mogadishu.
events.why: The IRC links the rain to El Niño, which usually brings wetter October to December rains to the eastern Horn.

source.title: El Niño rains flood Mogadishu, disrupting health clinic operations

events.title: Kingston water hours cut as Mona Reservoir falls
events.impact: Mona Reservoir at 35.9%; from 17 September supply stops around 4 pm daily, and 99 of about 450 water systems are hit by drought.
events.why: The water company does not name El Niño; a dry late wet season in the Caribbean fits El Niño's usual pattern.
events.quote: 99 of the commission’s approximately 450 water supply systems are being affected by drought conditions, representing approximately 22 per cent of systems nationally

source.title: NWC tightens water supply for some customers as Mona Reservoir falls to 35.9%

events.title: Little to no rain across eastern Australian cropping regions
events.place: Cropping regions of New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland and South Australia
events.impact: Little to no rain fell across most cropping regions in NSW, Victoria, Queensland and South Australia in the week to 23 September; ABARES says later rain is likely too late to lift northern winter crops.
events.why: ABARES says El Niño keeps strengthening and typically brings drier springs to parts of eastern Australia, but does not blame it for this week's dry spell.
events.quote: Across cropping regions, rainfall was largely confined to Western Australia, with most south eastern and eastern cropping regions remaining mostly dry.

source.title: Weekly Australian Climate, Water and Agricultural Update, 24 September 2026
source.publisher: ABARES, Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry

events.title: Zimbabwe approves a drought plan ahead of a forecast dry season
events.impact: Cabinet expects 1.6 million tonnes of cereal, a shortfall of 266,881 to 541,881 tonnes, and targets a 600,000-tonne grain reserve.
events.why: Cabinet approved the plan because of a forecast very strong El Niño and below-normal rain. This is a plan, not an observed drought yet.
events.quote: in response to a forecast super El Niño expected to bring below-normal rainfall to Zimbabwe and the region

source.title: Cabinet okays 6-pillar drought mitigation plan

events.title: Brazil's Amazonas state declares a drought emergency
events.impact: Up to 648,000 people (162,000 families) in all 62 municipalities could be affected, says the state's 180-day drought emergency decree.
events.why: The decree cites El Niño forecasts of below-average rain and above-average heat into early 2027.

source.title: Amazonas decreta emergência por estiagem e prevê impacto em 648 mil pessoas

events.title: Medellín brings back night water cuts
events.place: Six comunas in north-east and central-east Medellín, Colombia
events.impact: Cuts from 8 pm to 4 am on alternate days from 22 September, after the Piedras Blancas reservoir fell from 91% to 76% in 15 days.
events.why: The head of the water company EPM says the situation is caused by El Niño.
events.quote: el esfuerzo todavía no alcanza frente a la situación causada por el fenómeno de El Niño

source.title: Habrá nuevos racionamientos de agua en Medellín desde este 22 de septiembre: importante embalse está con niveles de reserva críticas

events.title: PAGASA: 45 Philippine provinces already in dry conditions or drought
events.impact: 45 provinces hit by dry conditions, dry spell or drought as of 21 September, 26 of them in the Visayas; PAGASA expects up to 85 provinces by March 2027.
events.why: PAGASA links the dry conditions to a strong El Niño it expects to become very strong by the end of 2026.
events.quote: As of Sept. 21, 45 provinces across the country have already been affected by dry conditions, dry spell, and drought amid El Niño.

source.title: Drought, dry spell likely to hit 85 provinces until March 2027 amid El Niño (PAGASA)

events.title: Karnataka set to raise drought-hit taluks to 177
events.place: Karnataka, India, worst in South and North Interior Karnataka
events.impact: 36% rain deficit from June to September (642 mm against a normal 852 mm); drought-hit taluks set to rise to 177, possibly around 200.
events.why: The state's revenue minister told the Legislative Council that part of the rain shortfall is due to El Niño.
events.quote: He attributed part of the rainfall deficiency to El Nino conditions.

source.title: 177 Talukas in Karnataka Drought-Hit, Could Reach 200; Maharashtra May Face 100% Drought by September-End

events.title: Category 5 Hurricane Polo shuts ports on Mexico's Pacific coast
events.impact: Winds of 165 mph offshore; the navy shut ports in Guerrero and Michoacán, classes were suspended in some areas, and 8 to 15 cm of rain was forecast.
events.why: A Colorado State University hurricane scientist quoted by AP blames El Niño for the storm's rapid strengthening.
events.quote: attributed the intensification to the weather phenomenon known as El Niño, which has fueled crippling droughts in Mexico and Central America

source.title: Category 5 Hurricane Polo is 'one of the strongest storms ever'

events.title: Lima sets a September heat record
events.impact: 26.9 C on 22 September, a new September record per meteorologist Abraham Levy; Senamhi issued a red warning for more daytime heat through 25 September.
events.why: Infobae reports the record amid El Niño conditions, and Peru's El Niño committee expects above-normal coastal temperatures and possible new records this spring.
events.quote: En medio del escenario climático asociado al Fenómeno El Niño, Lima-Callao registró una temperatura inusual para septiembre.

source.title: Lima y Callao viven una tarde histórica de calor: registran 26,9 °C, la temperatura más alta para septiembre desde que hay registros

events.title: Tonga: Vava'u at high to critical drought, Niuatoputapu declared
events.impact: 24 September drought outlook: Vava'u at high to critical drought; Ha'apai, Tongatapu and 'Eua stay under a drought declaration; Niuatoputapu upgraded to a declaration; 80 to 100% chance of very dry September to November.
events.why: Tonga Meteorological Services links the drought to a strengthening El Niño.
events.quote: Tonga Meteorological Services says Vava’u is facing high to critical drought conditions and potentially prolonged dry weather linked to a strengthening El Niño event

source.title: Vava'u drought warning as El Niño strengthens

events.title: Out-of-season downpours overflow rivers on Ecuador's coast
events.place: Guayas, Los Ríos, Manabí and Esmeraldas, Ecuador
events.impact: 106 mm in 24 hours at Samborondón and 105.8 mm at Montalvo; six rivers overflowed, two in Guayas and four in Esmeraldas.
events.why: Ecuador's weather service names warm El Niño sea temperatures as a cause of the rain.
events.quote: la elevada temperatura de la superficie del mar por el Fenómeno de El Niño

source.title: Estos son los lugares en los que más llovió en la Costa entre el 26 y 27 de septiembre de 2026, según el Inmahi

events.title: Philippines: El Niño farm damage reaches 6.87 billion pesos
events.place: 14 regions of the Philippines (marker at Magat Dam, Cagayan Valley, where cloud seeding ran)
events.impact: More than 223,000 farmers and 249,028 hectares hit; 163,812 tonnes of output lost, mostly corn (126,883 t) and rice (25,196 t); figures still being validated.
events.why: The Department of Agriculture reports the losses as damage from the strong El Niño.
events.quote: The strong El Niño has inflicted P6.87 billion in agricultural damage across the country, hitting more than 223,000 farmers

source.title: El Niño deals P6.87-B blow to agriculture sector

events.title: Hurricane Nolo floods roads on Hawaii's Big Island
events.impact: About 400 National Guard members activated statewide as Nolo's rain flooded streets near Naalehu and closed parts of a main highway.
events.why: A National Weather Service forecaster says this above-average Pacific storm season fits El Niño years.

source.title: Hurricane Nolo skirts Hawaii, but powerful winds and flooding remain threats

events.title: Panama Canal raises Neopanamax draft to 49 ft and adds a daily slot as lake conditions improve
events.impact: Maximum Neopanamax draft back to 49.0 ft (from 48.0 ft) effective immediately; a tenth Neopanamax slot takes daily capacity from 32 to 33 for booking dates from 15 Oct.
events.why: The Canal Authority cites September rain in the watershed, water-saving measures and projected lake levels, and does not name El Niño; the restrictions it eases were attributed to the El Niño dryness.

source.title: Advisory to Shipping A-36-2026
